Sam — thanks for the clear list. Looping Lauren (commercial) and Hannah (product/optimize) so you get an integrated reply. High level answers first, then a proposed two-option commercial sketch.

Short answers:
- Billing & caching: prefix + KV caching reduce billable compute in the common case but do not change per-token accounting for source prompts stored in the client. Practically: cached KV hits avoid model compute and so lower per-word compute cost; our billing increments on model-invocation tokens consumed, so you will see a ~30–65% effective token-cost reduction in read-heavy chat flows depending on cache hit rate. We will provide an account-level hit-rate dashboard and rollout hooks.
- Quantization quality: for the 13B family we observe median latency improvements of ~2.4x on A100-ish hardware using 4-bit hybrid quantization, with negligible quality loss on standard prompts. Int8 gives bigger speedups but shows a measurable drop on edge-case completion diversity. Hannah — attaching a short quality note with numbers.

Commercial options (sketch):
Option A — Pilot credits + usage banding:
  • 6-week pilot: $25k credits (redeemable against token usage), 20% off list for first $50k of billable usage during pilot.
  • Post-pilot: 3-tier commit bands (monthly commit) with volume discounts: 0-200k tokens = list, 200k-1M tokens = 12% off, >1M tokens = 20% off.
Option B — Hybrid reserved + usage discount:
  • 3-month reserved baseline (prepay $40k) to secure dedicated slot reservations during peak windows.
  • Usage above baseline billed at 15% discount.

Attachments: our pricing worksheet and a short technical note on quant tradeoffs. Happy to refine; Lauren can run through concession thresholds.

Sam, quick technical summary and conservative guidance for production rollout.

1) Caching & billing nuance:
- Prefix caching: saves forward compute when the same prefix appears; this reduces compute billed because fewer decoder steps execute. We recommend enabling client-side deterministic prefix hashing so you can estimate hit-rates before switching on server-side caching.
- KV cache (session-level): great for chat continuity. We see hit rates of 55–80% for session-based customer support agents; when hit-rate >40% you typically cross the inflection where caching materially reduces net token cost.

2) Quantization recommendations:
- Start with 4-bit (NF4 or GPTQ-compatible) for generator workloads. Our in-house benchmarks on 13B variants show mean response BLEU/ROUGE/LL differences within 1.5% vs fp16 on standard conversational prompts; tail-case hallucination increases are small but visible on long-context retrieval synthesis.
- Int8 is well-suited for high-throughput embedding/encoder tasks and large-batch offline workloads. We do NOT recommend int8 on customer-facing generative flows without targeted evals.

3) Deployment guardrails and A/B plan:
- Canary quantized model behind routing policy; fallback to fp16 variant for >5% quality regression on your eval prompts.
- Add prompt-level scoring to detect drift and auto-switch to higher-precision model for low-confidence outputs.

I'll include a short eval checklist (attached) you can run during pilot; it contains 20 edge-case prompts to measure tail-behavior.

Hannah
